raw_text:
Great — below is a 12-week strength + hypertrophy programme tailored for a 26‑year‑old recreational female lifter on combined oral contraceptive (no need to phase around cycle). Start date: 2026‑06‑01. Programme aims: increase strength (focus on squat, deadlift, bench/press) and improve body composition (muscle mass + reduce fat). Assumptions: cleared for full intensity, training 4 days/week (can be adjusted to 3 or 5 if you tell me), access to barbell, dumbbells, bench, squat rack, cables/rows, and cardio options. Progression uses linear loading with weekly and block progression, deload week every 4th week. Nutrition and recovery guidance follows.

Overview & structure
- Duration: 12 weeks, divided into three 4‑week phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Hypertrophy-strength base — higher volume, moderate loads (8–12 RM / 6–8 RM).
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength emphasis — lower reps, heavier loads (4–6 RM) with maintained hypertrophy work.
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Intensification & peak — heavier singles/low reps in main lifts + accessory hypertrophy, plus a final week to test/assess.
- Frequency: 4 sessions/week (Upper/Lower split, 2× each). Typical week:
  - Day 1: Lower A (strength focus)
  - Day 2: Upper A (strength focus)
  - Day 3: Lower B (hypertrophy/accessory)
  - Day 4: Upper B (hypertrophy/accessory)
- Tempo: Controlled eccentric ~2–3s, pause/transition 0–1s, concentric explosive as appropriate.
- Rest: Main lifts 2–4 minutes between top sets in strength weeks; accessories 60–90s.
- Progression: Add weight when top set reps are achieved across prescribed sets for two consecutive sessions, or add 2.5–5% to bar for upper/lower respectively. If unable to progress, repeat workload one more session then reduce load if failing repeatedly.
- Deload: Week 4 and Week 8 are moderate deloads (volume reduction ~30–40% or prescribed lighter loads).

Testing & targets
- Baseline 1RM estimates (recommended to test or estimate in Week 0): squat, deadlift, bench press or overhead press. If you don’t want testing, use starting working weights ~70% of comfortable 1RM for phase 1 main lifts.
- Target: meaningful increases in barbell strength (e.g., 5–15% improvement depending on current level) and visible body-composition improvements with consistent nutrition.

Weekly template (detailed sessions)
Weeks 1–3: Phase 1 — Base hypertrophy-strength
- Training notes: moderate loads, higher volume for muscular hypertrophy and technique reinforcement.

Week 1 (2026-06-01 start) — Week 1 of 12
Day 1 — Lower A (Main strength focus)
1. Back squat — 4 sets × 6–8 reps (RPE 7–8). Build to top set at prescribed reps.
2. Romanian deadlift — 3 × 8–10
3. Bulgarian split squat — 3 × 8–10 per leg
4. Leg curl (lying or seated) — 3 × 10–12
5. Standing calf raise — 3 × 12–15
6. Core: Pallof press or planks — 3 × 30–60s

Day 2 — Upper A (Main strength focus)
1. Bench press (barbell) or dumbbell bench — 4 × 6–8
2. Bent-over barbell row or chest-supported row — 4 × 6–8
3. Seated dumbbell shoulder press — 3 × 8–10
4. Incline dumbbell fly or cable chest fly — 3 × 10–12
5. Lat pulldown or pull-up assistance — 3 × 8–10
6. Arm finisher: Triceps pushdown 2 × 12–15, Biceps curl 2 × 12–15

Day 3 — Rest or active recovery (light cardio, mobility)

Day 4 — Lower B (Hypertrophy/accessory)
1. Deadlift (conventional or trap bar) — 4 × 5–6 (moderate intensity)
2. Front squat or goblet squat — 3 × 8–10
3. Hip thrust — 3 × 8–10
4. Walking lunges — 3 × 10–12 steps each
5. Seated calf raise — 3 × 12–15
6. Core: Hanging knee raises or cable crunch — 3 × 12–15

Day 5 — Upper B (Hypertrophy/accessory)
1. Overhead press (barbell or dumbbell) — 4 × 6–8
2. Single-arm dumbbell row — 3 × 8–10 each
3. Incline bench press — 3 × 8–10
4. Face pulls — 3 × 12–15
5. Lateral raises — 3 × 12–15
6. Rear delt machine or banded pull-apart — 2 × 15–20

Day 6–7 — Rest / optional low-impact cardio (20–30 min easy walk/cycle) and mobility.

Weeks 2–3: Repeat the Week 1 template for Weeks 2 and 3, increasing load modestly when hitting the top of rep ranges for main lifts. Aim to add ~1.25–2.5 kg to upper-lift increments, 2.5–5 kg to lower-lift increments as appropriate.

Week 4: Deload week (volume ~60–70% of normal)
- Reduce top sets and total sets by ~30–40% or use 60% of usual working weights for 3 sets of main lifts at 5–6 reps. Keep technique and mobility focus. Light accessory work only.

Weeks 5–7: Phase 2 — Strength emphasis
- Shift rep ranges down on main lifts; add heavier singles/double work on the final week of the phase. Maintain accessory hypertrophy to preserve muscle mass.

Week 5 (Start of Phase 2)
Day 1 — Lower A
1. Back squat — 5 × 4–6 (work up to challenging weight)
2. Romanian deadlift — 4 × 6–8
3. Bulgarian split squat — 3 × 6–8
4. Nordic hamstring or hamstring curl — 3 × 8–10
5. Calves — 3 × 10–12
6. Core: Cable anti-rotation — 3 × 8–10 each side

Day 2 — Upper A
1. Bench press — 5 × 4–6
2. Bent-over row — 4 × 6–8
3. Weighted pull-ups or lat pulldown — 3 × 6–8
4. Seated dumbbell press — 3 × 6–8
5. Triceps dips or close grip bench — 3 × 8–10
6. Biceps 2 × 10–12

Day 3 — Rest / active recovery

Day 4 — Lower B
1. Deadlift (conventional/trap) — 5 × 3–5 (heavier; build over sets)
2. Front squat or pause squat — 3 × 6–8
3. Hip thrust — 4 × 6–8
4. Walking lunges or step-ups — 3 × 8–10
5. Calf work — 3 × 12–15
6. Core: Planks + anti-extension drills — 3 × 30–60s

Day 5 — Upper B
1. Overhead press — 4 × 4–6
2. Dumbbell row — 3 × 6–8 each
3. Incline bench — 3 × 6–8
4. Face pulls — 3 × 12–15
5. Lateral raises / rear delt — 3 × 12–15
6. Arm superset (curl + triceps extension) — 2 × 10–12

Weeks 6–7: Continue similar structure. Increase loads on main lifts weekly if top sets hit reps. Aim to increase intensity each week, but monitor technique. Week 8 will be the next deload.

Week 8: Deload week
- Reduce load/volume ~30–40%: main lifts 3 sets × 3–5 at ~60% of usual working weight. Keep mobility, foam rolling, and light cardio. Use this week to recover before Phase 3.

Weeks 9–11: Phase 3 — Intensification & peak
- Main lifts: heavier singles/doubles/triples early in the week, accessory hypertrophy maintained. Increase intensity and include some AMRAP (as many reps as possible) sets for progress checks.

Week 9
Day 1 — Lower A
1. Back squat — 4 sets: 1 × heavy double (RPE 8–9), 2 × 2–3, 1 × back-off 5 (use lighter)
2. Deadlift variation (Romanian) — 3 × 6
3. Paused split squat — 3 × 6 each
4. Hamstring curl — 3 × 8–10
5. Calves — 3 × 10–12
6. Core: Hanging leg raises — 3 × 10–12

Day 2 — Upper A
1. Bench press — 4 sets: 1 × heavy double, 2 × 2–3, 1 × back-off 6–8
2. Bent-over row — 4 × 4–6
3. Weighted chin-ups/pulldowns — 3 × 6–8
4. Dumbbell shoulder press — 3 × 6–8
5. Face pulls — 3 × 12–15
6. Arms — 2 × 10–12

Day 4 — Lower B
1. Deadlift (trap bar or conventional) — 4 × 3 (heavier)
2. Front squats — 3 × 3–5
3. Hip thrust — 4 × 6–8 (heavy)
4. Bulgarian split squats — 3 × 8
5. Calf + core work

Day 5 — Upper B
1. Overhead press — 4 × 3–5
2. Incline bench — 3 × 5–6
3. Single-arm row — 3 × 8 each
4. Lateral raises + face pulls — 3 × 12–15 each
5. Arm work: 2–3 sets

Week 10
- Continue heavy focus: replace one main lift session with an AMRAP set on a compound lift (e.g., bench AMRAP at 75–80% x as many reps to monitor progress).
- Keep accessory volume moderate.

Week 11
- Peak week: attempt near-maximal singles on main lifts for testing if desired (safely, with spotters and proper warm-up). Otherwise continue heavy triples/doubles and one AMRAP set.

Week 12: Test & deload-ish / transition week
- Day 1 — Test squat 1RM (or heavy single) after full warm-up; then light accessory work.
- Day 2 — Test bench press 1RM; light accessory.
- Day 3 — Rest/mobility.
- Day 4 — Test deadlift 1RM (or wait until Day 5 if fatigue). Keep accessory minimal.
- The last week should be arranged so testing sessions are separated by at least 48 hours and you have spotters. If you prefer submax testing, do 3RM or 5RM tests instead.

Example progression (how to increase each week)
- Phase 1: add 1–2.5 kg per week to upper lifts when hitting rep ranges; 2.5–5 kg for lower lifts.
- Phase 2: add 1–2.5 kg per week; if stuck, repeat week then reduce rep range/back off.
- Phase 3: progress via heavier singles/doubles; use conservative jumps (1–2.5 kg for upper, 2.5–5 kg for lower).

Accessory selection & purpose
- Hamstrings (RDL, hamstring curl) to support deadlift and posterior chain development.
- Glute focus (hip thrust, Bulgarian split) for improved hip extension and aesthetics.
- Upper back (rows, face pulls) to balance pressing and improve posture.
- Rotator cuff and scapular work (face pulls, band pull-aparts) to reduce injury risk.
- Core anti-rotation/extension/anti-flexion drills to build transfer to big lifts.

Conditioning
- Optional 2 short cardio sessions per week (15–25 min), low-moderate intensity (walks, bike, row) on rest days or after lifting for extra calorie burn. Use high-intensity intervals sparingly on heavy weeks.

Nutrition guidance (general; not medical advice)
- Estimate maintenance calories (trainer to calculate from client). For body composition change:
  - Mild caloric deficit of ~200–350 kcal/day for fat loss while preserving muscle with resistance training (aim for ~0.3–0.6% bodyweight loss/week).
  - Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight/day (aim toward 2.0 g/kg for preserving/gaining lean mass in deficit).
  - Carbohydrates: moderate to high around training sessions to support performance (2–4 g/kg depending on total calories).
  - Fats: make up remainder, at least 20–25% of calories for hormonal health.
- Nutrient timing: prioritize a carbohydrate + protein meal ~1–2 hours pre-workout and a protein-rich meal or shake within 1 hour post-workout (20–40 g protein).
- Hydration: aim for consistent hydration; ~2–3 L/day baseline, more on hot days/training days.

Recovery & other recommendations
- Sleep: 7–9 hours/night.
- Mobility: daily short mobility session (10–15 min), targeted at hips, thoracic spine, shoulders.
- Soft tissue work: foam rolling once or twice weekly as needed.
- Deloads: follow scheduled deload weeks to reduce injury risk and consolidate gains.
- Monitoring: track training loads, reps, bodyweight, and subjective recovery (RPE, sleep, stress). Adjust calories or volume if strength stalls for several weeks.

Safety & contraindications
- Since the client is on combined OCP and asymptomatic around withdrawal bleeds, no cycle-based adjustments are necessary.
- Always cue proper technique, especially for heavy lifts. Use spotters for heavy bench/squat singles or use safety pins.
- If any joint pain or sharp pain arises, regress load or exercise and refer to medical professional.

Optional modifications
- If client prefers 3 sessions/week, use full-body sessions focusing on the same lifts (e.g., squat, hinge, push, pull each session with rotating variety).
- If client wants additional hypertrophy focus, add a 5th light session of targeted muscle groups or increase accessory sets.

Sample week-by-week quick summary
- Weeks 1–3: 4×/week upper-lower, 4×6–8 main lifts, higher accessory volume.
- Week 4: deload.
- Weeks 5–7: reduce reps on main lifts (5×4–6), increase intensity.
- Week 8: deload.
- Weeks 9–11: heavy singles/doubles, AMRAP tests, peak intensity.
- Week 12: testing 1RMs or heavy 3–5RMs; transition to new program after reassessment.

If you want, I can:
- Customize exact starting weights based on current lifts or estimated 1RMs.
- Convert the plan to 3 or 5 days/week.
- Provide a sample calorie and macronutrient plan based on her bodyweight and goals.
- Give an accessible printable/week-by-week table or a Google Sheets template to track loads.

Which would you like next?
